big_picture_notes: Exodus recounts Israel's deliverance from Egyptian slavery through ten plagues and the exodus event, the establishment of the Sinai covenant and God's law, and the construction of the tabernacle as God's dwelling place among His people. The book traces a theological arc from bondage to liberation to covenant community, establishing themes of redemption, law, and God's presence that echo throughout Scripture.

stories.story_title: The Deliverance: From Bondage to Wilderness
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Begins with Israel's oppression under a new Egyptian king (1:1). Ends with Jethro's visit affirming Moses' leadership and God's deliverance (18:27). The entire section is framed by the pattern: bondage→need→God's provision→instruction. Literary devices: generational structure (Joseph's generation fades, Moses' generation rises), multiplication motif (Israel multiplies despite oppression), repeated complaint-provision cycles (water, food, enemy), and the development of Moses from refugee to leader. This story establishes both the problem (slavery) and its resolution (God's deliverance and community formation).

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the book by naming the 70 who came down (bridge from Genesis 46). Ends at the total count. Devices: Genealogical inclusio linking Exodus to Genesis; 'seventy souls' echoes the table of nations.
Starts as the founding generation dies. Ends with the land 'filled.' Devices: Five fertility verbs (fruitful, increased, multiplied, grew, filled) echo the creation/Noah blessing.

scenes.scene_name: A New King Who Did Not Know Joseph
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the ominous new king. Ends with Pharaoh's 'let us deal shrewdly.' Devices: Dramatic irony; the king's fear drives the plot; 'lest they multiply' fights God's blessing.

Starts with forced-labor taskmasters. Ends with 'their lives bitter.' Devices: The more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied (counter-intuitive growth); store-cities Pithom and Rameses named.
Starts with Pharaoh's secret order to Shiphrah and Puah. Ends with the midwives sparing the boys. Devices: Civil disobedience rooted in fear of God; named women vs. unnamed Pharaoh.
Starts with Pharaoh's interrogation. Ends with God giving the midwives households. Devices: Irony (the 'vigorous Hebrew women' explanation); reward for reverence.

scenes.scene_name: Pharaoh's Command to Drown the Boys
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A single-verse hinge: genocide by the Nile. Devices: The Nile (Egypt's life-source) made an instrument of death—foreshadows Plague 1 and the Red Sea.

scenes.scene_name: The Birth and Hiding of Moses
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with a Levite marriage and birth. Ends with the sister watching the basket. Devices: 'She saw he was good' (tov) echoes creation; the 'ark' (tevah) is the same word as Noah's.
Starts with Pharaoh's daughter at the river. Ends with the naming of Moses. Devices: Reversal (Pharaoh's own house saves the deliverer); pun on Mosheh / 'drawn out.'
Starts with Moses going out to his people. Ends with 'surely this is known.' Devices: 'Who made you ruler and judge?' ironically anticipates his true calling; failed premature deliverance.
Starts with Pharaoh seeking Moses' life. Ends with Moses defending the shepherd-daughters. Devices: Betrothal type-scene at a well (cf. Isaac, Jacob); Moses again the deliverer of the weak.
Starts with Reuel's question. Ends with the birth of Gershom, 'a stranger there.' Devices: Naming etymology; Moses' exile identity as a sojourner.
Starts with the king of Egypt's death. Ends with 'God knew.' Devices: Fourfold divine response (heard, remembered, saw, knew); covenant remembrance turns the plot toward rescue.
Starts at Horeb, the mountain of God. Ends with Moses hiding his face. Devices: The bush burning unconsumed (theophany); 'holy ground'; the covenant-name 'God of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob.'
Starts with 'I have surely seen.' Ends with 'bring my people out.' Devices: 'I have come down' (divine descent); the land 'flowing with milk and honey'; commission of Moses.

scenes.scene_name: The Name Revealed: I AM WHO I AM
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Moses' 'Who am I?' Ends with the memorial name YHWH. Devices: Objection-and-reassurance pattern; 'I AM' (ehyeh) wordplay; the name 'forever.'

scenes.scene_name: Commission to the Elders and Pharaoh
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'Go, gather the elders.' Ends with the promise that God's wonders will compel release. Devices: Scripted speech; foreknowledge of Pharaoh's hard heart; 'mighty hand.'

scenes.scene_name: The Plunder of the Egyptians Foretold
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'I will give this people favor.' Ends with 'you will plunder the Egyptians.' Devices: Reversal of the oppressed into the enriched; fulfillment flagged for 12:35-36.
Starts with Moses' 'they will not believe me.' Ends with the first sign given. Devices: Sign authentication; the staff (shepherd's tool) becomes a weapon of God.

scenes.scene_name: The Leprous Hand and the Nile Sign
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the second sign (leprous hand). Ends with the third sign (Nile to blood). Devices: Escalating triad of signs; blood-on-dry-land foreshadows Plague 1.
Starts with 'I am slow of speech.' Ends with 'please send someone else.' Devices: The reluctant-prophet motif; Moses' final evasion provokes God's anger.
Starts with the LORD's anger kindled. Ends with 'take this staff.' Devices: Concession (Aaron the mouth, Moses as 'God' to him); the staff commissioned for signs.
Starts with Moses asking Jethro's leave. Ends with Moses taking the staff of God. Devices: 'Those who sought your life are dead' (echo of Jacob/Joseph); the family journey begins.
Starts with the LORD's instructions en route. Ends with the threat to Pharaoh's firstborn. Devices: 'I will harden his heart'; the firstborn motif set up for Plague 10.
Starts with the LORD seeking to kill Moses at the lodging place. Ends with Zipporah's circumcision rite. Devices: Cryptic night-attack; blood and circumcision avert death (Passover foreshadow).
Starts with Aaron sent to meet Moses. Ends with the people bowing in worship. Devices: The signs performed; the people 'believe'—a high point before the coming collapse.
Starts with 'Let my people go.' Ends with Pharaoh's 'you make them rest from their labors.' Devices: 'Who is the LORD?'—Pharaoh's central question the plagues will answer.
Starts with Pharaoh's order to the taskmasters. Ends with 'pay no regard to lies.' Devices: Tyranny intensifies under the demand for freedom; oppression as policy.
Starts with the taskmasters relaying the order. Ends with the foremen beaten. Devices: Bureaucratic cruelty; the impossible demand exposes the system.
Starts with the Israelite foremen appealing to Pharaoh. Ends with 'you are in trouble.' Devices: Appeal-and-rebuff; the people's hope curdles.

scenes.scene_name: Moses Cries Out to the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the foremen confronting Moses. Ends with Moses' 'why have you brought trouble?' Devices: Lament/complaint to God; the deliverer questions his commission.

scenes.scene_name: I Am the LORD; I Remember My Covenant
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'Now you will see.' Ends with 'I have remembered my covenant.' Devices: Self-revelation formula; El Shaddai vs. the name YHWH; covenant memory.

Starts with 'Say to the Israelites: I am the LORD.' Ends with 'I am the LORD.' Devices: Sevenfold redemption verbs (bring out, deliver, redeem, take, be your God, bring in, give); inclusio on the Name.
Starts with the people's refusal from 'broken spirit.' Ends with the charge to Pharaoh. Devices: 'Uncircumcised lips' objection returns; despair as obstacle.

scenes.scene_name: Heads of the Fathers' Houses: Reuben, Simeon, Levi
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'These were the heads of their fathers' houses.' Ends with Levi's years. Devices: Genealogy inserted to credential Moses and Aaron before the Pharaoh confrontation resumes; only the first three tribes listed (the goal is Levi).

scenes.scene_name: The Line of Levi to Moses and Aaron
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Levi's sons (Gershon, Kohath, Merari). Ends with Amram and Jochebed bearing Aaron and Moses. Devices: Narrowing genealogy zooms to the deliverers; Amram's marriage named.

scenes.scene_name: The Sons of Izhar, Aaron, and Korah
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Izhar's sons. Ends with Phinehas among 'the heads of the Levite families.' Devices: Aaron's marriage and sons (Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, Ithamar); Korah noted (foreshadows Numbers 16).

scenes.scene_name: These Are the Aaron and Moses
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'It was this Aaron and Moses.' Ends restating their commission to bring Israel out. Devices: Inclusio closing the genealogy and resuming the narrative thread.
Starts with 'On the day the LORD spoke.' Ends with Moses' renewed objection. Devices: Resumptive repetition (picking up after the genealogy); the speech-impediment motif.

scenes.scene_name: I Have Made You Like God to Pharaoh
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'See, I have made you like God.' Ends with 'the Egyptians will know I am the LORD.' Devices: Prophet/mouthpiece role formalized; the 'knowing' refrain that structures the plagues.
Starts with their obedience. Ends with their ages (80 and 83). Devices: Obedience formula; age notice frames the deliverer generation.

scenes.scene_name: The Staff Becomes a Serpent Before Pharaoh
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the sign command. Ends with Pharaoh's hardened heart. Devices: Contest with the magicians; Aaron's staff swallows theirs—foreshadows the outcome.

scenes.scene_name: Plague 1 Announced: The Nile to Blood
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Pharaoh's heart 'unyielding.' Ends with the prophetic threat. Devices: Confrontation at the water's edge; the Nile-god targeted.
Starts with the command to stretch out the staff. Ends with the stench of dead fish. Devices: Totalizing language ('all the waters'); the river of life becomes death.
Starts with the magicians replicating it. Ends with seven days passing. Devices: Counterfeit power; Pharaoh's indifference; time-stamp closes the episode.
Starts with 'Let my people go.' Ends with the frogs entering Pharaoh's house. Devices: The threat invades the palace and bedchamber—personal, total.
Starts with Aaron's outstretched hand. Ends with the magicians copying it. Devices: The counterfeit makes things worse, not better—escalation of folly.

scenes.scene_name: Pharaoh Begs; Moses Sets the Time
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Pharaoh's first plea ('entreat the LORD'). Ends with 'so you may know there is no one like the LORD.' Devices: First crack in Pharaoh; 'tomorrow'—Moses lets Pharaoh choose, proving God's control.
Starts with Moses crying out. Ends with the hardened heart 'as the LORD had said.' Devices: Relief brings relapse—the pattern that will repeat.
Starts with no warning—dust to gnats. Ends with the magicians' confession, 'This is the finger of God.' Devices: First plague the magicians cannot copy; turning point in the contest.
Starts at the water in the morning. Ends with the land 'ruined' by flies. Devices: First distinction—Goshen spared; 'so you may know I am the LORD in the land.'
Starts with Pharaoh's 'sacrifice within the land.' Ends with Moses' warning not to deal falsely. Devices: Negotiation/compromise tactic; Moses insists on the three-day journey.
Starts with Moses' prayer. Ends with Pharaoh hardening his heart again. Devices: The relapse refrain seals the episode.
Starts with 'Let my people go.' Ends with the appointed time ('tomorrow'). Devices: Distinction promised between Egypt's and Israel's herds; scheduled judgment.
Starts with the plague falling. Ends with Pharaoh's heart unmoved. Devices: Sharp contrast ('not one of Israel's animals died'); investigation that changes nothing.
Starts with the soot thrown skyward. Ends with the LORD hardening Pharaoh's heart. Devices: The magicians cannot even stand—their final disappearance; first time the LORD (not Pharaoh) hardens.

scenes.scene_name: Plague 7 Announced: 'I Will Send My Plagues'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'early in the morning.' Ends with Pharaoh still exalting himself. Devices: Theological climax—'that my name be proclaimed in all the earth'; purpose of the plagues stated.

scenes.scene_name: Warning to Shelter from the Hail
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the unprecedented hail foretold. Ends with the God-fearing vs. heedless Egyptians. Devices: Mercy within judgment—those who 'feared the word' could be saved.
Starts with the outstretched staff. Ends with Goshen spared. Devices: Fire and ice together ('hail with fire flashing'); cosmic disorder; the distinction holds.
Starts with 'This time I have sinned.' Ends with Moses' 'I know you do not yet fear God.' Devices: The fullest confession yet—and Moses' shrewd disbelief.

scenes.scene_name: The Hail Stops; Pharaoh Sins Again
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the ruined flax and barley. Ends with the hardened heart. Devices: Agricultural note (what survived sets up the locusts); the relapse refrain.
Starts with 'I have hardened his heart...that you may tell your children.' Ends with Moses storming out. Devices: Generational memory purpose; threat of total devouring.
Starts with Pharaoh's officials ('Egypt is ruined!'). Ends with Moses and Aaron driven out. Devices: Pharaoh's compromise—'only the men go'; cracks in his own court.
Starts with the east wind. Ends with 'nothing green remained.' Devices: Wind as God's instrument (foreshadows the Red Sea wind); totalizing devastation.
Starts with Pharaoh's hurried summons. Ends with the LORD hardening his heart. Devices: Repentance-relapse cycle; a west wind drives the locusts into the sea.
Starts with the outstretched hand. Ends with light in all Israel's dwellings. Devices: 'Darkness that can be felt' (un-creation, anti-Genesis); the sun-god eclipsed; the distinction at its starkest.
Starts with Pharaoh's last bargain (leave the flocks). Ends with 'you will never see my face again.' Devices: Negotiation collapses; the threshold to the final plague.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Promises One Last Plague
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'One more plague.' Ends with Moses' high regard in Egypt. Devices: Narrative aside; the favor/plunder promise nears fulfillment.

Starts with 'About midnight.' Ends with Moses leaving in hot anger. Devices: The decisive threat; from Pharaoh's firstborn to the slave-girl's—total leveling; the dog 'not even barking' marks the distinction.
Starts with 'Pharaoh will refuse.' Ends with the hardened heart. Devices: Summary refrain closing the plague cycle; 'that my wonders may be multiplied.'
Starts with 'This month shall be the beginning.' Ends with the twilight slaughter. Devices: New calendar (new beginning); the lamb 'without blemish,' kept and then killed by 'the whole assembly.'

scenes.scene_name: Eat It in Haste: Blood and Bread
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the blood on the doorposts. Ends with 'it is the LORD's Passover.' Devices: Apotropaic blood; roasted lamb, bitter herbs, unleavened bread; readiness to flee ('loins girded').
Starts with 'I will pass through Egypt.' Ends with the festival 'as a lasting ordinance.' Devices: Judgment 'on all the gods of Egypt'; the blood as 'a sign'; memorial command.
Starts with 'Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.' Ends with the rule for foreigner and native. Devices: Leaven purged (haste/holiness); 'cut off' formula; sacred assemblies bracket the week.
Starts with Moses summoning the elders. Ends with the destroyer passing over. Devices: The hyssop and basin; instruction handed from God to Moses to the people.

scenes.scene_name: A Lasting Ordinance for the Children
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'Observe this rite.' Ends with the people bowing and obeying. Devices: Catechesis ('When your children ask...'); obedience formula closes the unit.

scenes.scene_name: The Death of the Egyptian Firstborn
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'At midnight the LORD struck.' Ends with Pharaoh's 'Go...and bless me also.' Devices: The threat fulfilled to the letter; 'a loud wailing'; total surrender.

scenes.scene_name: Egypt Urges Israel Out; The Plunder
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the Egyptians urging haste. Ends with 'they plundered the Egyptians.' Devices: Dough without leaven (the haste motif); the favor/plunder promise fulfilled (cf. 3:21-22).
Starts with the march of 'about 600,000 men.' Ends with the unleavened cakes baked in haste. Devices: Census-scale notice; the 'mixed multitude'; bread of affliction explained.
Starts with the length of the sojourn. Ends with 'a night of vigil for all generations.' Devices: Chronological inclusio; the night kept by the LORD and by Israel in return.
Starts with 'This is the statute.' Ends with 'the whole congregation must celebrate it.' Devices: Membership rules (no foreigner uncircumcised); one lamb, one house, no broken bone.
Starts with the resident-alien provision. Ends with the exodus 'by their divisions.' Devices: 'One law' for native and stranger; closing march-out formula.
Starts with 'Consecrate to me every firstborn.' Devices: Brief divine command; the firstborn claim flows from Plague 10—they are now the LORD's.
Starts with 'Remember this day you came out.' Ends with the seven-day unleavened rule. Devices: Memory imperative; 'no leaven seen among you'; the land-promise tied to the rite.
Starts with 'You shall tell your son.' Ends with 'keep this ordinance.' Devices: Catechesis again; sign on hand and forehead (frontlets); annual observance.
Starts with entry into the land. Ends with the sign 'on your hand and forehead.' Devices: Firstborn of beast and man redeemed; child's question answered ('with a mighty hand').

scenes.scene_name: God Leads by Pillar of Cloud and Fire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the route that avoids the Philistines. Ends with the pillar never departing. Devices: Divine guidance; Joseph's bones carried (Genesis promise kept); cloud by day, fire by night.

scenes.scene_name: Encamp by the Sea: A Trap Set
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'Turn back and encamp.' Ends with 'I will gain glory over Pharaoh.' Devices: God lures Pharaoh; the 'knowing' refrain; the trap is intentional.
Starts with Pharaoh's change of heart. Ends with the chariots overtaking Israel by the sea. Devices: 600 chosen chariots; the hardened heart drives him to the trap.

scenes.scene_name: Israel's Terror; 'The LORD Will Fight for You'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Israel's cry of fear. Ends with 'be still.' Devices: Murmuring motif begins; Moses' faith-speech; the paradox of salvation through stillness.
Starts with 'Why are you crying to me?' Ends with the glory-over-Egypt purpose. Devices: From prayer to action; the staff over the sea; honor through Pharaoh's army.

scenes.scene_name: The Pillar Moves; The Sea Divides
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the angel and pillar shifting to the rear. Ends with the waters 'a wall on their right and left.' Devices: The cloud as barrier (darkness to Egypt, light to Israel); the east wind divides the sea (cf. creation waters).
Starts with the Egyptians pursuing into the sea. Ends with 'not one of them survived.' Devices: God 'threw them into confusion'; the wheels clog; the waters return—reversal of the crossing.

scenes.scene_name: Israel Saved; They Feared and Believed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Israel walking through on dry ground. Ends with the people fearing the LORD and believing Moses. Devices: Closing inclusio (dry ground); 'Israel saw'—faith born from deliverance.

scenes.scene_name: The Song of the Sea: 'The LORD Is a Warrior'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'I will sing to the LORD.' Ends with the foes sinking 'like a stone.' Devices: Victory hymn; 'The LORD is a warrior, the LORD is his name'; vivid sea imagery.

scenes.scene_name: Your Right Hand Shattered the Enemy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic.' Ends with the enemy sinking 'like lead.' Devices: Anthropomorphic power (right hand, blast of nostrils); the boast of the enemy answered by a breath.

scenes.scene_name: Who Is Like You, O LORD?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'Who among the gods is like you?' Ends with God leading to 'your holy dwelling.' Devices: Incomparability formula; transition from past rescue to future guidance.

scenes.scene_name: The Nations Tremble; The LORD Reigns
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the peoples hearing and trembling. Ends with 'The LORD reigns forever and ever.' Devices: Future conquest anticipated (Edom, Moab, Canaan); the sanctuary-mountain; royal acclamation.
Starts with the recap of Pharaoh's horses. Ends with Miriam's antiphon. Devices: Female prophet leads with timbrel; refrain repeats the song's opening—musical inclusio.

scenes.scene_name: Bitter Water at Marah; Rest at Elim
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with three days without water. Ends with the twelve springs of Elim. Devices: First wilderness test; the sweetened wood (sign); 'I am the LORD who heals you'; rest-stop reward.
Starts in the Wilderness of Sin. Ends with 'you have brought us out to kill us with hunger.' Devices: Murmuring motif intensifies; nostalgia for Egypt's 'pots of meat.'
Starts with 'I will rain down bread.' Ends with 'your grumbling is against the LORD.' Devices: The daily-portion test; grumbling redirected from Moses to God.

scenes.scene_name: The Glory Appears; Quail and Manna
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the assembly before the LORD. Ends with 'you will know I am the LORD your God.' Devices: Theophany in the cloud; the 'knowing' refrain; provision as revelation.
Starts with the evening quail and morning dew. Ends with 'everyone gathered as much as he needed.' Devices: The naming question (man hu); the omer measure; equity miracle (no lack, no excess).
Starts with Moses' command not to hoard. Ends with the manna melting in the sun. Devices: Test of trust; the rotting/worms judgment on hoarding.

scenes.scene_name: A Double Portion for the Sabbath
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the sixth-day double gathering. Ends with 'on the seventh there will be none.' Devices: Sabbath introduced before Sinai; the manna that keeps overnight (reversal of the daily rule).
Starts with some going out to gather anyway. Ends with the people resting. Devices: Disobedience and rebuke; 'the LORD has given you the Sabbath'—gift framed as rest.
Starts with the description of manna. Ends with the omer measure explained. Devices: Memorial jar 'before the Testimony'; forty-years note (proleptic); closing measurement gloss.

scenes.scene_name: No Water at Rephidim; The People Quarrel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the journey to Rephidim. Ends with 'Why did you bring us up to kill us with thirst?' Devices: Quarrel (rib) motif; the thirst test repeats Marah at higher pitch.

scenes.scene_name: Water from the Rock at Massah and Meribah
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Moses' 'they are ready to stone me.' Ends with the place-names 'Massah and Meribah.' Devices: The struck rock; God 'standing on the rock'; the testing question, 'Is the LORD among us?'
Starts with Amalek's attack. Ends with Joshua overwhelming them. Devices: First war; Moses' raised hands (the staff of God) tip the battle; Aaron and Hur support him—intercession dramatized.
Starts with 'Write this on a scroll.' Ends with 'the LORD will be at war with Amalek.' Devices: Memorial writing; the altar 'The LORD Is My Banner' (YHWH-Nissi).
Starts with Jethro hearing all God had done. Ends with his arrival message to Moses. Devices: Outsider/priest of Midian honors the LORD; the sons' names (Gershom, Eliezer) recapped.

scenes.scene_name: Jethro Rejoices and Worships the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the warm reunion. Ends with the sacrificial meal before God. Devices: Gentile confession ('Now I know the LORD is greater than all gods'); fellowship sacrifice with the elders.
Starts with Moses judging from morning to evening. Ends with 'I make known the statutes of God.' Devices: Sets up the problem; the lone-mediator bottleneck.

scenes.scene_name: Jethro's Counsel: Teach Them the Way
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'What you are doing is not good.' Ends with 'show them the way to live.' Devices: Wise critique; the principle of teaching and delegation.
Starts with 'select capable men who fear God.' Ends with 'this people will go home in peace.' Devices: Tiered judiciary (thousands, hundreds, fifties, tens); criteria of character.
Starts with Moses listening to his father-in-law. Ends with Jethro's departure. Devices: Obedience to wise counsel; transition note closing the deliverance arc before Sinai.

stories.story_title: The Sinai Covenant: Law, Instruction, and Community Formation
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Begins with Israel arriving at Sinai (19:1). Ends with covenant ratified through blood sacrifice and Moses entering God's presence on mountain (24:18). The entire section establishes God's covenantal relationship with Israel through law. Literary structure: Theophany (God's awesome descent) → Law (God's instruction and expectations) → Covenant ratification (community's commitment and God's sealed promise). This story moves Israel from freed slaves to covenanted community with defined identity and obligations. Central motif: 'I will be your God, you will be my people' (19:5-6).

scenes.scene_name: Arrival at Sinai; Eagles' Wings; a Kingdom of Priests
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts in the third month at Sinai. Ends with 'a kingdom of priests, a holy nation.' Devices: Eagles'-wings metaphor; the covenant proposal that frames all of Sinai.

scenes.scene_name: Moses Relays the Words; The People Consent
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Moses setting the words before the elders. Ends with 'all the people answered together.' Devices: Covenant call-and-response; the LORD will come 'in a dense cloud.'

scenes.scene_name: Consecration: Wash, Wait, and Keep the Bounds
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'consecrate them today and tomorrow.' Ends with the three-day readiness. Devices: Ritual preparation; the deadly boundary around the mountain heightens holiness.

scenes.scene_name: The Theophany: Thunder, Trumpet, and Smoke
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts on the morning of the third day. Ends with God answering in thunder. Devices: Sensory overload (thunder, lightning, trumpet, smoke, quaking) — Sinai as a volcano of holiness.
Starts with the LORD calling Moses up. Ends with Moses going down to warn the people. Devices: Repeated boundary warning; tension between access and danger.

scenes.scene_name: I Am the LORD; You Shall Have No Other Gods
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'And God spoke all these words.' Ends with the first commandment. Devices: Self-identification by the redemption from Egypt grounds the law in grace before demand.

scenes.scene_name: No Idols; Do Not Misuse the Name
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the prohibition of images. Ends with the third commandment. Devices: Jealous-God formula; visiting iniquity vs. showing love to thousands.
Starts 'Remember the Sabbath.' Ends grounding it in creation. Devices: The longest commandment; creation rationale ties Sinai back to Genesis 2.
Starts with honoring father and mother. Ends with 'you shall not covet.' Devices: The second-table commandments; from outward acts to the inward heart (covetousness).

scenes.scene_name: The People Tremble; Moses Draws Near
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the people seeing the thunder and trembling. Ends with Moses approaching the thick darkness. Devices: Fear and mediation; 'do not be afraid... that the fear of him may be before you.'

scenes.scene_name: The Altar Law: Earth and Unhewn Stone
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'You have seen that I spoke from heaven.' Ends with the rule against steps to the altar. Devices: Opens the Book of the Covenant; simple altar guards against idolatry and pride.
Starts 'These are the ordinances.' Ends with the servant 'for life.' Devices: Case-law form; the seventh-year release echoes the Sabbath; the pierced ear as a sign of love.

scenes.scene_name: The Rights of a Female Servant
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the daughter sold as a servant. Ends with her going free without payment. Devices: Protective legislation; her food, clothing, and marital rights guaranteed.
Starts with 'whoever strikes a man.' Ends with cursing father or mother. Devices: 'A place to flee' (cities of refuge foreshadowed); life-for-life seriousness.

scenes.scene_name: Injury in a Quarrel; Striking a Servant
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with men quarreling. Ends with the servant 'his property.' Devices: Restitution principle; lost-time compensation; limits on a master's power.

scenes.scene_name: Harm to a Pregnant Woman; Eye for Eye
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the struggle harming a pregnant woman. Ends with freeing a servant for a knocked-out tooth. Devices: The lex talionis ('eye for eye') — measured, limiting retribution.
Starts with the ox that gores a person. Ends with the price for a servant. Devices: Graduated liability based on prior warning; the ox stoned, the owner accountable.

scenes.scene_name: Liability for a Pit and a Goring Ox
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the uncovered pit. Ends with the ox-for-ox rule. Devices: Negligence law; restitution restores the neighbor, not merely punishes.
Starts with stealing an ox or sheep. Ends with double restitution for what is found alive. Devices: Restitution scaled to the crime; the thief restores, even fivefold.

scenes.scene_name: Damage to Fields and by Fire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with grazing in another's field. Ends with fire that spreads. Devices: 'Best of his own field' restitution; accountability for spreading harm.
Starts with goods given for safekeeping. Ends with 'pay double to his neighbor.' Devices: 'Brought before the judges'; the oath before God resolves the unseen.
Starts with an animal entrusted that dies or strays. Ends with the torn carcass as evidence. Devices: The oath of the LORD between the two parties; honesty under God.
Starts with a borrowed animal injured. Ends with the hired animal's case. Devices: Brief liability rule distinguishing borrowing from hiring.

Starts with seducing an unbetrothed woman. Ends 'whoever sacrifices to any god must be destroyed.' Devices: Moral and cultic boundaries together; the sorceress and the idolater under the same severity.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Oppress the Foreigner, Widow, or Orphan
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Do not mistreat a foreigner.' Ends with God's burning anger. Devices: Memory of Egypt as motive ('you were foreigners'); God as defender of the defenseless.
Starts with lending without interest. Ends with 'I am compassionate.' Devices: Mercy in economics; the cloak returned by sunset; God's character grounds the law.

scenes.scene_name: Reverence, Firstfruits, and a Holy People
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Do not blaspheme God or curse a ruler.' Ends 'you are to be my holy people.' Devices: Firstborn and firstfruits given to God; holiness expressed in diet.

scenes.scene_name: Justice: No False Reports or Partiality
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Do not spread a false report.' Ends with not favoring the poor in a lawsuit. Devices: Impartiality cuts both ways — neither crowd nor pity may bend justice.

scenes.scene_name: Help Your Enemy; Pervert No Justice
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with returning an enemy's stray ox. Ends 'you know how it feels to be a foreigner.' Devices: Love of enemy embedded in law; bribery and oppression forbidden.

scenes.scene_name: The Sabbath Year and Sabbath Day
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the seventh-year rest for the land. Ends with not invoking other gods. Devices: Rest for land, servant, and animal; the Sabbath rhythm woven through creation and society.
Starts 'Three times a year.' Ends 'do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.' Devices: Unleavened Bread, Harvest, Ingathering; firstfruits to the house of the LORD.

scenes.scene_name: The Angel Sent to Guard the Way
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'I am sending an angel ahead of you.' Ends with the angel bringing them in. Devices: 'My Name is in him'; obedience tied to guidance and conquest.

scenes.scene_name: Serve the LORD Alone; Blessings Promised
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with not bowing to their gods. Ends with full lifespans and no miscarriage. Devices: Exclusive worship rewarded with bread, water, health, and fruitfulness.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Send My Terror; Little by Little
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'I will send my terror.' Ends 'little by little I will drive them out.' Devices: The hornet; gradual conquest 'until you have increased' — providence paced to readiness.

scenes.scene_name: Boundaries Set; Make No Covenant with Them
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the borders from sea to river. Ends 'they will be a snare to you.' Devices: Land-promise boundaries; separation from idolatry as self-protection.
Starts with the call to come up with the elders. Ends 'everything the LORD has said we will do.' Devices: Graded access to God; the people's first ratifying word.
Starts with Moses writing the words and building an altar. Ends 'the blood of the covenant.' Devices: Blood split between altar and people; 'we will do and we will obey'; covenant sealed.

scenes.scene_name: The Elders See God and Eat
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the seventy going up. Ends 'they saw God, and they ate and drank.' Devices: Theophanic meal; the sapphire pavement; remarkable nearness without harm.

scenes.scene_name: Moses Called Up for the Tablets
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Come up to me and stay.' Ends with Aaron and Hur left in charge. Devices: The stone tablets promised; the delegation that sets up the golden-calf crisis.

scenes.scene_name: The Glory on Sinai; Moses Enters the Cloud
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the cloud covering the mountain. Ends with forty days and nights. Devices: 'Like a consuming fire'; the six-day wait then the seventh-day call — the long absence begins.

stories.story_title: The Dwelling Instructions: God's House Among His People
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Begins with 'The LORD said to Moses: Tell the Israelites to bring me an offering' (25:1). Ends with God's specifications complete and priesthood consecration detailed (31:18). This story provides detailed architectural and liturgical instructions for the tabernacle—God's portable dwelling place. Literary structure: Freewill offering (community participation) → Sacred structure details (ark, table, lampstand, altar) → Priestly garments and consecration → Observance instructions (Sabbath, incense). Central theme: 'I will dwell among you' (29:45-46)—God's presence moves from mountain-distant to community-centered.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Calls for an Offering
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the tabernacle instructions. Ends 'from everyone whose heart prompts him.' Devices: Freewill giving — the sanctuary built from willing hearts, not taxation.
Starts listing gold, silver, bronze. Ends with the onyx and gemstones. Devices: The catalog of materials anticipates the finished glory; precious things devoted to God.

scenes.scene_name: Make Me a Sanctuary by the Pattern
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Have them make a sanctuary for me.' Ends 'according to the pattern.' Devices: 'That I may dwell among them' — the theological heart of Exodus; the heavenly pattern.
Starts with the ark's dimensions. Ends with the gold rings. Devices: The most holy object described first; gold inside and out.
Starts with the carrying poles. Ends 'put the Testimony into the ark.' Devices: Poles never removed (readiness to move); the ark houses the covenant words.

scenes.scene_name: The Mercy Seat and the Cherubim
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the atonement cover of pure gold. Ends 'there I will meet with you.' Devices: The cherubim facing the cover; the meeting-place between the cherubim — the focal point of the whole sanctuary.

scenes.scene_name: The Table of Acacia and Gold
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the table's dimensions. Ends with its four rings. Devices: Parallel construction to the ark; the furniture of God's house.

scenes.scene_name: The Utensils and the Bread of the Presence
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the rings and poles. Ends 'the bread of the Presence...always before me.' Devices: Perpetual bread signifies continual fellowship and provision.

scenes.scene_name: The Golden Lampstand: Branches and Cups
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the hammered-gold lampstand. Ends with the branches of one piece. Devices: Almond-blossom cups (organic, tree-like form); light in the holy place.

scenes.scene_name: The Lamps and the Pattern on the Mountain
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the seven lamps. Ends 'according to the pattern shown you.' Devices: A talent of pure gold; the refrain of the heavenly pattern closes the unit.

scenes.scene_name: The Ten Curtains of the Tabernacle
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the fine linen curtains and cherubim. Ends with the gold clasps joining them into one. Devices: 'One tabernacle' — unity from many parts; woven cherubim echo the ark.
Starts with the goat-hair tent over the tabernacle. Ends with the loops along the edges. Devices: Layered coverings; the protective tent over the sacred dwelling.
Starts with the bronze clasps. Ends with the ram-skin and goatskin coverings. Devices: Plain outside, glory inside — the hidden beauty of God's house.
Starts with the upright frames. Ends with the twenty frames for the south side. Devices: The skeleton of the structure; standing boards of acacia overlaid with gold.

scenes.scene_name: The Silver Bases for the South
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the forty silver bases. Ends with two bases per frame. Devices: Silver foundations (from the census redemption money) bear the whole structure.

scenes.scene_name: Frames for the West and the Corners
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the rear frames. Ends with the sixteen bases. Devices: Cornering details ensure a stable, square dwelling.

scenes.scene_name: The Crossbars; Set Up by the Plan
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the acacia crossbars. Ends 'set up the tabernacle according to the plan.' Devices: The center bar running end to end; the pattern-refrain again.

scenes.scene_name: The Veil and the Ark Within
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the veil of blue, purple, scarlet. Ends with the table and lampstand placed. Devices: The veil separates Holy from Most Holy; spatial theology of access.
Starts with the entrance screen. Ends with its five bronze bases. Devices: The threshold curtain; graded holiness from courtyard inward.
Starts with the altar of burnt offering. Ends with the bronze grating. Devices: Horns on the four corners; the place where sacrifice meets the worshiper.
Starts with the altar's poles. Ends 'make it hollow, like a box.' Devices: Portability again; the pattern shown on the mountain.

scenes.scene_name: The Courtyard: South, North, and West
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the courtyard hangings. Ends with the east side's width. Devices: Linen walls define sacred space; the enclosure that frames worship.

scenes.scene_name: The Gate and the Bronze Pegs
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the hangings flanking the gate. Ends with all the pegs of bronze. Devices: The single, colorful gate — one way in; bronze throughout the court.
Starts with clear pressed-olive oil. Ends 'a lasting ordinance for the generations.' Devices: Aaron tends the lamp from evening to morning — perpetual light before the LORD.

scenes.scene_name: Aaron and His Sons Set Apart
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with calling Aaron and his sons to serve. Ends with the materials for the garments. Devices: 'For glory and beauty'; the priesthood instituted; named sons.
Starts with the ephod of gold and fine linen. Ends with its waistband. Devices: The priest's central vestment; artistry as worship.

scenes.scene_name: The Onyx Stones and Gold Chains
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the two onyx stones. Ends with the braided chains. Devices: The twelve tribal names engraved 'as a memorial' — the priest carries Israel on his shoulders.
Starts with the breastpiece. Ends with the first rows of stones. Devices: Worn over the heart; 'judgment' anticipates the Urim and Thummim.
Starts with the remaining rows. Ends 'one for each of the twelve tribes.' Devices: Each tribe a distinct jewel — Israel precious and named before God.

scenes.scene_name: The Chains and Rings of the Breastpiece
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the braided chains. Ends with fastening to the ephod. Devices: Goldsmith detail binding heart-piece to shoulder-piece.

scenes.scene_name: The Memorial and the Urim and Thummim
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the lower rings. Ends 'over his heart before the LORD continually.' Devices: The means of divine guidance carried on the priest's heart.

scenes.scene_name: The Robe of the Ephod and Its Bells
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the blue robe. Ends 'so that he will not die.' Devices: Pomegranates and bells — sound signals the priest's living service in the holy place.

scenes.scene_name: The Gold Plate: Holy to the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the engraved gold plate. Ends with the sash. Devices: 'HOLY TO THE LORD' on the forehead — the priest bears the guilt of the holy gifts.
Starts with tunics for the sons. Ends 'a lasting ordinance.' Devices: Linen undergarments for modesty before God; holiness in every detail.
Starts 'This is what you are to do to consecrate them.' Ends with washing at the tent entrance. Devices: A bull, two rams, unleavened bread; the ordination begins with cleansing.

scenes.scene_name: Vesting and Anointing Aaron and His Sons
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with putting on the garments. Ends 'the priesthood is theirs by a lasting ordinance.' Devices: Robing and anointing oil — investiture of the priesthood.
Starts with the bull at the tent. Ends with burning it outside the camp. Devices: Hands laid on the head (transfer); blood on the horns; atonement inaugurated.

scenes.scene_name: The First Ram: A Burnt Offering
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the first ram. Ends 'a pleasing aroma to the LORD.' Devices: Whole burnt offering — total dedication ascending to God.

scenes.scene_name: The Second Ram: Ear, Thumb, and Toe
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the ordination ram. Ends with sprinkling oil and blood. Devices: Blood on ear, thumb, toe — consecrating hearing, action, and walk.
Starts with the fat and the bread. Ends 'a pleasing aroma to the LORD.' Devices: The wave gesture before God; portions burned on the altar.

scenes.scene_name: The Priests' Portion; Garments Passed Down
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the breast as Moses' share. Ends with the seven-day vesting of the successor. Devices: Provision for the priests; continuity of office across generations.
Starts with boiling the ram's meat. Ends with burning leftovers. Devices: A sacred meal at the tent entrance; only the consecrated may eat the holy food.

scenes.scene_name: Seven Days; The Altar Made Holy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the seven-day ordination. Ends 'whatever touches the altar will be holy.' Devices: Sevenfold completeness; contagious holiness of the atoning altar.

scenes.scene_name: The Daily Offerings: Morning and Evening
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'This is what you are to offer regularly.' Ends with the evening lamb. Devices: The perpetual lamb bracketing each day — continual communion.
Starts with the meeting place at the tent. Ends 'I am the LORD their God.' Devices: The climactic promise of indwelling; the purpose of the exodus restated — 'that I might dwell among them.'
Starts with the incense altar of acacia and gold. Ends with its poles. Devices: Placed before the veil; the smaller golden altar of prayer.
Starts with its position before the ark. Ends 'most holy to the LORD.' Devices: Morning-and-evening incense; the once-a-year atonement on its horns links it to the Day of Atonement.

scenes.scene_name: The Census Tax: A Half Shekel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the census ransom. Ends with the atonement money for the tent. Devices: 'No plague'; rich and poor give the same — equal value before God; funds the silver bases.
Starts with the basin between tent and altar. Ends 'a lasting ordinance.' Devices: Washing hands and feet before service — 'so that they will not die'; cleansing precedes ministry.
Starts with the finest spices. Ends 'a sacred anointing oil.' Devices: Myrrh, cinnamon, cane, cassia — a holy perfume set apart by precise measure.
Starts with anointing the tent and ark. Ends 'whatever touches them will be holy.' Devices: Consecration by oil; the spreading holiness motif again.

scenes.scene_name: The Sacred Oil Not for Common Use
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with anointing Aaron and his sons. Ends with being 'cut off.' Devices: The oil reserved exclusively for the holy — boundary between sacred and common.
Starts with the fragrant spices. Ends 'must be cut off.' Devices: A unique recipe 'most holy'; imitation for personal use forbidden — holiness is not to be cheapened.

scenes.scene_name: Bezalel and Oholiab Filled with the Spirit
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'I have chosen Bezalel.' Ends with the gift of skill to all the able. Devices: The first person 'filled with the Spirit of God' — Spirit-empowered craftsmanship and wisdom.

scenes.scene_name: Their Commission: All the Sacred Work
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts listing the tent and furnishings. Ends 'they are to make them just as I commanded.' Devices: The full inventory entrusted to the artisans; obedience to the pattern.
Starts 'You must observe my Sabbaths.' Ends 'he rested.' Devices: The Sabbath as the covenant sign bracketing the tabernacle instructions; creation-rest rationale.
A single-verse hinge: the finger of God writes the tablets. Devices: 'Inscribed by the finger of God' — the climax of the mountain encounter; sets up the descent into the calf crisis.

stories.story_title: The Breach and Renewal: Covenant Broken and Restored
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Begins with 'When the people saw that Moses delayed coming down from the mountain' (32:1). Ends with covenant renewal and God's presence reaffirmed on mountain with renewed tablets (34:35). This story narrates Israel's covenant violation (Golden Calf idolatry) and God's merciful restoration. Literary structure: Breach (Israel's rebellion, gods created) → Judgment (God's wrath, Levite execution) → Intercession (Moses' prayer preserves remnant) → Renewal (covenant remade, God's character revealed). Central irony: While Moses receives law on high, Israel violates it below; yet God's grace exceeds wrath, and covenant continues despite breach.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A single-verse trigger: 'Make us gods who will go before us.' Devices: Moses' delay breeds idolatry; the crisis erupts the instant the instructions end.
Starts with collecting the gold earrings. Ends 'they rose up to revel.' Devices: 'These are your gods, O Israel'; corrupted worship mimics the real festival — a parody of Sinai.
Starts 'Go down, your people have corrupted themselves.' Ends 'I will make you into a great nation.' Devices: God disowns them to Moses ('your people'); the offer that tests Moses' heart.
Starts with Moses pleading. Ends 'the LORD relented.' Devices: Moses argues from God's reputation and the patriarchal promise — intercession that bends the outcome.

scenes.scene_name: The Tablets Broken; the Calf Burned
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Moses descending with the tablets. Ends with the people drinking the ground gold. Devices: The shattered tablets dramatize the broken covenant; humiliating destruction of the idol.
Starts with Moses confronting Aaron. Ends 'out came this calf!' Devices: Comic, evasive self-justification — leadership abdicated.

scenes.scene_name: The Levites Rally to the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the people running wild. Ends 'you have been set apart.' Devices: 'Whoever is for the LORD, come to me'; costly loyalty ordains the Levites.

scenes.scene_name: Moses' Plea: 'Blot Me Out'; the Plague
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'You have committed a great sin.' Ends with the LORD striking the people. Devices: Substitutionary plea ('blot me out of your book'); judgment tempered but not erased.

scenes.scene_name: Go Up, but I Will Not Go With You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the command to leave for the land. Ends 'lest I destroy you on the way.' Devices: The terrible mercy — the gift of the land without the Giver; raises the book's deepest question of Presence.

scenes.scene_name: The People Mourn and Strip Their Ornaments
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the people mourning the 'distressing word.' Ends with them stripping off their ornaments at Horeb. Devices: Repentance enacted; the jewelry that made the calf now laid aside.

scenes.scene_name: The Tent of Meeting; Face to Face
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Moses pitching the tent outside the camp. Ends 'the LORD would speak to Moses face to face.' Devices: The pillar at the entrance; Joshua remaining — intimacy with God amid estrangement.
Starts with Moses' bold petition. Ends 'I will do the very thing you ask.' Devices: The argument that Presence is what distinguishes Israel; 'I know you by name' — favor secured.

scenes.scene_name: Show Me Your Glory; Hidden in the Rock
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Show me your glory.' Ends 'you will see my back.' Devices: The cleft of the rock; God's goodness passing by — the limits and grace of seeing God.
Starts 'Cut two tablets like the first.' Ends with Moses ascending at dawn. Devices: Covenant renewal begins; Moses now provides the stone — a new start after the breach.

Starts with the LORD descending in the cloud. Ends 'yet he does not leave the guilty unpunished.' Devices: The great self-revelation — 'compassionate and gracious, slow to anger' — the most quoted creed in the Old Testament.

scenes.scene_name: Moses Bows and Pleads for the Presence
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Moses bowing low. Ends 'take us as your inheritance.' Devices: Worship flows straight into intercession; he pleads on the basis of the revealed name.

scenes.scene_name: A Covenant of Wonders; Tear Down Their Altars
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'I am making a covenant.' Ends 'smash their sacred stones.' Devices: Renewed promise of wonders; demolition of rival worship as covenant fidelity.

scenes.scene_name: Worship No Other God; No Intermarriage
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Do not worship any other god.' Ends with the danger of their daughters. Devices: 'The LORD, whose name is Jealous'; idolatry framed as marital betrayal.

scenes.scene_name: No Idols; Feasts and the Firstborn
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Do not make idols.' Ends 'no one is to appear before me empty-handed.' Devices: The renewed covenant restates the festivals and the firstborn claim.

scenes.scene_name: Sabbath, Festivals, and the Three Appearances
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Six days you shall labor.' Ends with the promise that none will covet the land. Devices: Sabbath even in plowing and harvest; the three pilgrim feasts; providence guards the empty borders.

scenes.scene_name: Festival Laws; Forty Days; the Ten Words Written
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the festival rules. Ends 'he wrote the Ten Commandments.' Devices: Forty days without bread or water; the covenant words re-inscribed — restoration complete.
Starts with Moses descending with the tablets. Ends with him giving the commands. Devices: His face shines from being with God; Aaron and the people afraid to come near.
Starts with Moses veiling his face. Ends with the recurring practice. Devices: The veil on and off — closeness to God leaves a visible mark (cf. 2 Cor 3).

stories.story_title: The Dwelling Construction: Covenant Community Builds
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Begins with 'Moses assembled the whole Israelite community' (35:1). Ends with 'the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle' (40:34). This story narrates the actual construction and assembly of the tabernacle according to specifications. Literary structure: Sabbath rest reminder and offering call → Community's freewill contribution → Craftspeople's construction of components (coverings, frames, furniture, vessels) → Assembly in proper sequence → Glory's descent (God's presence visible). Central theme: covenant community participates in God's dwelling place through unified effort. Inclusio: 'I will dwell among you' (29:45) → 'the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle' (40:34).

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Moses assembling the people. Ends 'do not light a fire on the Sabbath.' Devices: Even sacred building yields to the Sabbath; the rhythm framed the instructions and now frames the work.
Starts 'Take from among you an offering.' Ends with the gemstones. Devices: 'Everyone who is willing'; the materials list echoes ch. 25 — willing hearts again.

scenes.scene_name: Let the Skilled Come: The Furnishings Listed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Let every skilled craftsman come.' Ends with the lampstand and oil. Devices: The construction inventory recited; gifted hands invited to the work.

scenes.scene_name: The Altar, Court, and Garments Listed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the incense altar. Ends with the priestly garments. Devices: Completing the catalog; the whole sanctuary previewed before it is built.
Starts with the people withdrawing, then returning. Ends with the offerings brought. Devices: 'Everyone whose heart stirred him' — generosity as worship; the reversal of the gold given to the calf.

scenes.scene_name: The Women Spin; A Freewill Gift
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the skilled women spinning. Ends 'a freewill offering to the LORD.' Devices: Named contribution of the women; men and women together; willing hearts emphasized.

scenes.scene_name: Bezalel and Oholiab Gifted to Teach
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'See, the LORD has chosen Bezalel.' Ends 'master craftsmen and designers.' Devices: Spirit-filled skill repeated; the gift 'to teach others' — craftsmanship multiplied.
Starts with the craftsmen at work. Ends with the people bringing more each morning. Devices: The community's overflow; gifts received 'morning after morning.'
Starts with the craftsmen reporting the surplus. Ends 'the people were restrained from giving.' Devices: The only place in Scripture giving must be stopped — generosity beyond need.
Starts with making the linen curtains. Ends with joining them into one. Devices: Obedient execution mirrors the ch. 26 command word for word — the pattern realized.
Starts with the goat-hair curtains. Ends with the ram-skin and goatskin coverings. Devices: The layered tent built exactly as instructed.

scenes.scene_name: The Frames and Silver Bases Made
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the upright frames. Ends with the south-side bases. Devices: The structure assembled to specification; silver from the redemption money bearing the weight.
Starts with the north-side frames. Ends with the sixteen bases. Devices: Methodical, repetitive faithfulness — the text lingers on obedience.
Starts with the acacia crossbars. Ends with overlaying them in gold. Devices: The center bar; the skeleton of the dwelling completed.

scenes.scene_name: The Veil and the Entrance Screen Made
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the veil of blue, purple, scarlet. Ends with the entrance screen and its bases. Devices: The dividing veil and threshold built — graded holiness realized.
Starts 'Bezalel made the ark.' Ends with the poles inserted. Devices: The named craftsman builds the holiest object; command becomes accomplishment.

scenes.scene_name: The Mercy Seat and Cherubim Made
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the atonement cover. Ends with the cherubim facing each other. Devices: The meeting-place fashioned in gold; the wings overshadowing the cover.
Starts with the table's dimensions. Ends with its rim. Devices: The furniture of the holy place made to plan.
Starts with the rings and poles. Ends with the pure-gold dishes. Devices: The vessels for the bread of the Presence completed.
Starts with the hammered-gold lampstand. Ends 'of one piece with it.' Devices: Almond cups and branches realized; light fashioned for the holy place.
Starts with the seven lamps. Ends 'a talent of pure gold.' Devices: Brief completion note; precious metal devoted.

scenes.scene_name: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Oil
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the incense altar. Ends with the anointing oil and pure incense. Devices: The golden altar and sacred compounds prepared by the perfumer's art.
Starts with the altar of burnt offering. Ends with its bronze utensils. Devices: The great altar built to specification; horns on its corners.
Starts with the bronze grating. Ends 'he made the altar hollow.' Devices: Portability detail; faithful to the pattern.

scenes.scene_name: The Bronze Basin from the Mirrors
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A single-verse note: the basin made from the women's mirrors. Devices: Vanity-objects transformed into vessels of cleansing — a small, vivid act of devotion.
Starts with the south-side curtains. Ends with the west-side hangings. Devices: The linen enclosure built; sacred space defined.
Starts with the east-side width. Ends with the hangings flanking the gate. Devices: The single entrance completed — one way into the court.
Starts with all the curtains of fine linen. Ends 'all the tent pegs were bronze.' Devices: The finishing hardware; every detail accounted for.
Starts 'These are the amounts.' Ends naming the craftsmen. Devices: A formal audit of the work; Ithamar oversees; the artisans credited.
Starts with the gold total. Ends with the half-shekel count. Devices: Precise accounting; the census tax visibly funds the bases — transparency in the holy work.
Starts with the silver for the bases. Ends with the bronze pegs. Devices: Every talent allocated; stewardship recorded down to the peg.
Starts 'From the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.' Ends 'as the LORD had commanded Moses.' Devices: The garments built; the refrain 'as the LORD commanded' begins its drumbeat.
Starts with the engraved onyx stones. Ends 'as the LORD had commanded Moses.' Devices: The tribal names set; obedience refrain repeated.
Starts with the breastpiece. Ends with the first row of stones. Devices: The judgment-piece fashioned to plan.
Starts with the second row. Ends 'each engraved like a seal...for the twelve tribes.' Devices: Israel's tribes set as jewels over the heart.
Starts with the braided chains. Ends with fastening to the ephod's shoulder pieces. Devices: Goldsmith work uniting the vestments.
Starts with the lower rings. Ends 'as the LORD had commanded Moses.' Devices: The breastpiece secured over the heart; refrain repeated.
Starts with the woven robe. Ends with bells and pomegranates 'as the LORD had commanded Moses.' Devices: The sound of ministry realized; refrain.

scenes.scene_name: The Tunics and the Holy Crown
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the linen tunics. Ends with 'HOLY TO THE LORD' on the turban. Devices: The priestly wardrobe finished; the holy diadem completed.

scenes.scene_name: The Work Finished; Brought to Moses
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'So all the work was completed.' Ends with the lampstand and its lamps. Devices: 'Just as the LORD had commanded' — the people obeyed; the finished work paraded before Moses (echoes Genesis 'God finished').

scenes.scene_name: Moses Inspects and Blesses the Work
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the remaining furnishings. Ends 'so Moses blessed them.' Devices: Inspection mirrors creation's 'God saw...it was good'; the blessing over completed obedience.

scenes.scene_name: Set Up the Tent; Place the Ark and Table
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'Set up the tabernacle on the first day.' Ends with arranging the lampstand. Devices: The command to assemble on New Year's Day — a new creation begins.
Starts with the incense altar. Ends with setting up the courtyard. Devices: The order of assembly from inside out; the dwelling made ready.

scenes.scene_name: Anoint the Tabernacle and Its Furnishings
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the anointing oil. Ends with consecrating the altar and basin. Devices: Everything made holy by oil before use — consecration precedes service.
Starts with washing Aaron and his sons. Ends 'Moses did everything just as the LORD commanded.' Devices: The priesthood installed; the obedience refrain marks the whole chapter.
Starts on the first day of the first month. Ends with spreading the tent over it. Devices: The literal raising; 'as the LORD had commanded Moses.'

scenes.scene_name: The Ark, Table, and Bread Placed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the Testimony into the ark. Ends with the bread set out. Devices: The furniture installed in order; obedience refrain repeated.

scenes.scene_name: The Lampstand and Incense Altar Set
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the lampstand. Ends with burning fragrant incense. Devices: Light and prayer established in the holy place; refrain repeated.

scenes.scene_name: The Screen, Altar, Basin, and Court Finished
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the entrance screen. Ends 'so Moses finished the work.' Devices: The final assembly completed; 'Moses finished' echoes the Genesis creation close.
Starts with the cloud covering the tent. Ends 'the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.' Devices: The climax of Exodus — God moves in; even Moses cannot enter the filled Presence.

scenes.scene_name: The Cloud and Fire Guide Israel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with the cloud lifting for the journeys. Ends 'in the sight of all Israel.' Devices: The book closes with God present and guiding — cloud by day, fire by night, all the way to the Promised Land.
